canonical_question: What specific mechanism allows Ti and Al peaks to disappear after only 1 hour, and does this imply rapid surface diffusion or bulk lattice dissolution?

question_variants.question: What specific mechanism allows Ti and Al peaks to disappear after only 1 hour, and does this imply rapid surface diffusion or bulk lattice dissolution?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The disappearance of Ti and Al peaks after 1 hour is attributed to the successful mechanical alloying of the Al element into the total content. The text does not explicitly distinguish between surface diffusion and bulk lattice dissolution mechanisms.

answers.answer: The Al element was successfully mechanically alloyed to the other powders in its total content already after 1 h, evidenced by the absence of the peaks of this element in XRD.
answers.mechanism: mechanical alloying resulting in total content integration
answers.boundary_limitation: specific mechanism (surface vs bulk) not detailed
evidence_spans: The sintering was performed on selected powders subject to different milling times, namely 3, 10, 30 and 50 h.
The milled powders were consolidated by spark plasma sintering technology (Sumitomo Coal Mining, Dr. Sinter SPS machine) using a graphite die with an inner diameter of 12 mm in a vacuum atmosphere.

The sintering was carried out at a constant uniaxial pressure of 50 MPa applied by die pistons at a maximum temperature of 1200 °C and a heating rate of 100 °C·min −1 up to 50 °C from the maximum sintering temperatures.
